newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia shares end lower, extending losing streak.
newsitem.headline: Colombia shares end lower, extending losing streak.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended lower for the sixth consecutive session in trading that saw movers selling across the board, brokers said.

"In a speculative market you can make a lot or lose a lot," one Bogota-based broker quipped when asked about the relentless losing streak. "Since people are seeing declines they're getting panicky and selling," he said.

Medellin's IBOMED general price index fell 1.30 percent to end at 17,892.15 on a trading volume of about 4.3 billion pesos. Bogota's IBB index shed 0.96 percent, meanwhile, ending the week at 1,180.21 on volume of just over 3.1 billion pesos.

Losers were everywhere but they were led by giants like Compania Suramericana de Seguros, Colombia's largest insurer, which fell 1.02 percent in Bogota to settle at 28,900 pesos per share. Banco de Bogota, the country's third biggest bank in terms of assets, gave up 0.92 percent in Bogota, where it ended at 6,400 pesos per share.

Blue-chip Bavaria SA fell 0.89 percent in Bogota and 0.83 percent in Medellin, ending in both centers at 7,750 pesos a share. "The market is a seller and when that happens there's not much you can do," one broker said in an interview.
